name: Sydney Opera House
clues: White concrete shells, all cut from one imaginary sphere, sit on a harbour point. Its architect resigned mid-build and never came back to see it finished.
blurb: The sails are covered in more than a million Swedish-made tiles that clean themselves when it rains. Utzon's winning entry was little more than a set of sketches.

name: Eiffel Tower
clues: Built as a temporary gateway to a world's fair, this wrought-iron lattice was the tallest structure on Earth for 41 years.
blurb: Leading Parisian artists protested against this 'useless and monstrous' tower before it went up. It's repainted by hand roughly every seven years and grows about 15 cm on hot days as the iron expands.

name: Burj Khalifa
clues: Its Y-shaped plan is borrowed from a desert flower, and it has held the world height record since the day it opened.
blurb: At 828 m it's so tall you can watch the sun set at the base, take the lift up, and watch it set again. The spire alone is taller than many skyscrapers.

name: Colosseum
clues: Four storeys of arches held around 50,000 spectators; sailors worked the canvas awning that shaded them.
blurb: Under the arena floor ran a maze of tunnels and lifts that hoisted animals and scenery up through trapdoors. After Rome fell it served as a quarry, a fortress and even housing.

name: Taj Mahal
clues: A white marble tomb for a beloved wife at the end of a quartered garden on a river bank. Its four minarets lean slightly outwards, away from the dome.
blurb: Some 20,000 workers are said to have spent over two decades on the complex. The white marble changes colour through the day, from pinkish at dawn to milky white at noon.

name: Empire State Building
clues: An Art Deco tower thrown up in just over a year during the Depression. Its mast was meant to moor airships.
blurb: It rose at an astonishing four and a half storeys a week. It has its own ZIP code, and lightning hits it about 20 times a year.

name: Sagrada Família
clues: A basilica under construction since 1882. Its architect, knocked down by a tram, is buried in the crypt.
blurb: Asked why it was taking so long, Gaudí reportedly replied that his client was not in a hurry. Inside, the columns branch like trees into a stone forest.

name: St Basil's Cathedral
clues: Nine chapels under swirling, candy-painted onion domes, at the end of the most famous square in a northern capital.
blurb: Legend says Ivan the Terrible blinded the architects so they could never build anything as beautiful again (almost certainly untrue). The famous colours were added long after it was built.

name: Petronas Towers
clues: Twin towers on an eight-pointed Islamic star plan, joined by a two-storey skybridge at the 41st and 42nd floors.
blurb: From 1998 to 2004 they were the tallest buildings in the world. The skybridge isn't fixed rigidly to the towers, so it can slide as they sway.

name: Leaning Tower of Pisa
clues: A cathedral bell tower started on soft clay. Wars stopped work for nearly a century, which let the ground settle and probably saved it from falling over.
blurb: It began to lean while still being built, so the upper floors were made slightly taller on one side to compensate. Engineers spent 1990–2001 straightening it by about 40 cm.

name: Parthenon
clues: A marble Doric temple with almost no straight lines: the columns swell and the floor bows upwards to correct the eye.
blurb: It stood largely intact for 2,000 years until 1687, when a Venetian cannonball hit gunpowder stored inside. Many of its sculptures now live in the British Museum.

name: Elizabeth Tower (Big Ben)
clues: A Gothic Revival clock tower on a riverside parliament. The name everyone uses really belongs to the 13-tonne bell inside.
blurb: The great bell cracked soon after it was hung and still rings slightly out of tune. Old pennies placed on the pendulum fine-tune the clock's timekeeping.

name: Forbidden City
clues: Nearly a thousand red-and-gold buildings behind a moat. For five centuries, ordinary people could not enter without the emperor's permission.
blurb: Legend says it has 9,999 rooms, one short of heaven's 10,000. Off-limits for nearly 500 years, it's now one of the most visited places on Earth.

name: Notre-Dame de Paris
clues: A Gothic cathedral on a river island, with flying buttresses and rose windows. Its 19th-century spire fell in a 2019 fire and was rebuilt exactly.
blurb: Victor Hugo's novel about its hunchbacked bell-ringer helped save it from ruin in the 1800s. After the 2019 fire, it reopened in December 2024.

name: Pantheon
clues: Still the world's largest unreinforced concrete dome, nearly 1,900 years on, with an open eye at the top that lets the rain in.
blurb: It has been in use for almost 2,000 years, today as a church. When it rains, the water falls through the open eye and drains away through small holes in the floor.

name: CN Tower
clues: A concrete telecom tower on a lakeshore, with a glass floor 342 m up. It was the world's tallest free-standing structure for 32 years.
blurb: Thrill-seekers can walk around the outside of the main pod, strapped to a rail 356 m up. It's struck by lightning dozens of times a year.

name: Hagia Sophia
architect: Isidore of Miletus & Anthemius of Tralles
clues: A dome that seems to float on a ring of 40 windows. It has been a church, a mosque, a museum and a mosque again.
blurb: For nearly a thousand years it was the largest cathedral in the world. Its first dome collapsed after an earthquake in 558 and was rebuilt taller.

name: Marina Bay Sands
clues: Three 55-storey hotel towers carry a 340-metre 'park' across their roofs, with an infinity pool at the edge.
blurb: The rooftop pool is about 150 m long and sits some 200 m above the bay. The deck overhangs the north tower by about 65 m.

name: Guggenheim Museum Bilbao
clues: Titanium-clad curves on an old industrial riverfront. Its success gave a whole urban-regeneration strategy its name.
blurb: Gehry's team designed its curves with CATIA, software made for designing fighter jets. The titanium skin is less than half a millimetre thick and ripples like fish scales.

name: Neuschwanstein Castle
clues: A fairy-tale castle for a reclusive king, secretly built on a steel frame with central heating. He lived there for only 172 days.
blurb: Ludwig II paid for it from his own fortune, not the state's. It opened to paying visitors weeks after his mysterious death, and it inspired Disney's Sleeping Beauty Castle.

name: Fallingwater
clues: A weekend house whose concrete terraces cantilever straight out over a waterfall in the Appalachian woods.
blurb: The Kaufmann family expected a house with a view of their favourite waterfall; Wright put them right on top of it. The cantilevers sagged for decades until they were reinforced in 2002.

name: Villa Savoye
clues: A white box on thin columns outside a capital, built as a manifesto of five points. A car's turning circle shaped the ground floor.
blurb: The roof leaked so badly that the Savoye family complained bitterly for years. Today it's one of the most influential houses of the 20th century.

name: Chrysler Building
clues: A steel sunburst crown. Its spire was assembled in secret inside the top floors and hoisted out in 90 minutes to steal a height record.
blurb: Its gargoyles are steel eagle heads and radiator caps modelled on Chrysler cars. It was the world's tallest building for less than a year.

name: Lotus Temple
clues: A Bahá'í house of worship made of 27 free-standing marble 'petals', open to people of every faith.
blurb: It has no altar, no clergy and no sermons, yet it ranks among the most visited buildings in the world. Nine pools around it help keep the hall cool.

name: Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque
clues: More than 80 white marble domes, reflecting pools, and one of the largest hand-knotted carpets in the world inside.
blurb: Its main chandelier is one of the largest in the world. The carpet in the main prayer hall was hand-knotted by about 1,200 artisans.

name: Atomium
clues: Nine steel spheres arranged as an iron crystal magnified 165 billion times, built for a world's fair.
blurb: It was built to stand for six months and never came down. The top sphere holds a restaurant with a view over all of Brussels.

name: Alhambra
clues: The red hilltop palace-fortress of the last Muslim kingdom in Western Europe, with honeycomb stucco ceilings and a fountain carried by twelve lions.
blurb: Its name means 'the red one', after the colour of its walls. Inside, the walls are covered in Arabic poetry carved into the stucco.

name: Potala Palace
clues: Thirteen storeys of white and red walls climbing a hill at 3,700 m: for three centuries the winter palace of a line of spiritual leaders.
blurb: It has more than 1,000 rooms and sits about 3,700 m above sea level, so many visitors are out of breath before they reach the top.

name: Angkor Wat
clues: The largest religious monument on Earth. It faces west, and its five lotus-bud towers are mirrored in a vast moat.
blurb: Its sandstone blocks came from quarries tens of kilometres away, probably by canal. It's the centrepiece of Cambodia's national flag.

name: CCTV Headquarters
clues: Two leaning towers joined at the top and bottom into one continuous loop for a state broadcaster. Locals call it 'big pants'.
blurb: The loop's overhanging corner juts out about 75 m in mid-air. The irregular grid on the facade is densest where the structure works hardest.

name: Oslo Opera House
clues: Its white stone roof slopes down into a fjord, so anyone can walk straight up onto it.
blurb: Locals picnic, sunbathe and skateboard on its roof. The marble was quarried in Carrara, Italy.

name: Elbphilharmonie
clues: A glass crown shaped like waves, sitting on top of a brick cocoa warehouse in a port. The main hall is lined with 10,000 unique acoustic panels.
blurb: A curved escalator 82 m long carries you up through the old warehouse. Costs grew to about ten times the original budget, and Hamburg got a world-class concert hall.

name: Cathedral of Brasília
clues: Sixteen curved concrete columns reach up like hands, in a capital city drawn from scratch in the 1950s.
blurb: Most of the church sits below ground: you enter through a dark passage and emerge into a bright glass hall. Four bronze evangelists guard the entrance.

name: Taipei 101
clues: Stacked like bamboo in eight-floor segments, with a 660-tonne golden steel ball hanging inside to calm typhoon sway.
blurb: The giant damper ball is so popular it has its own cartoon mascots, the 'Damper Babies'. Its lifts were once the fastest in the world.

name: Habitat 67
clues: 354 prefabricated concrete boxes stacked like a hillside village for a world expo — a student's thesis made real.
blurb: Safdie wanted to give apartment dwellers a garden, so each unit's terrace is the roof of the one below. He still keeps an apartment there.

name: Kunsthaus Graz
clues: A blue acrylic blob with nozzle-shaped skylights, nicknamed 'the friendly alien', moored beside a red-roofed old town.
blurb: At night its skin becomes a giant low-resolution screen made of 930 fluorescent rings. The nickname stuck so well that the museum uses it too.

name: Heydar Aliyev Center
clues: A white surface that rises out of the plaza and folds over a cultural centre with almost no straight lines, near an inland sea.
blurb: There are almost no straight lines anywhere. The skin is made of thousands of panels, nearly every one a different shape.

name: National Parliament House (Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban)
clues: Massive concrete walls pierced by giant circles and triangles, standing in an artificial lake. Its architect died years before it was finished.
blurb: Building work stopped during Bangladesh's 1971 war of independence and resumed after it. Surrounded by water, the parliament seems to float.

name: Great Mosque of Djenné
clues: The largest mud-brick building in the world. Every year the whole town turns out in a festival to replaster it.
blurb: The palm-wood sticks poking out of its walls are built-in scaffolding for the yearly replastering festival. The current building dates from 1907, on a site used since the 13th century.

name: Hallgrímskirkja
clues: A concrete church whose stepped front imitates basalt columns formed by cooling lava, towering over a small capital.
blurb: At about 75 m, it's one of the tallest structures in Iceland. A statue of the explorer Leif Erikson, a gift from the USA, stands outside.

name: Niterói Contemporary Art Museum
clues: A flying saucer on a cliff, reached by a red serpentine ramp, looking across a bay at a much more famous city.
blurb: A single central column holds up the whole saucer. The view across Guanabara Bay frames Rio's Sugarloaf Mountain.

name: Church of St George (Bete Giyorgis)
architect: Commissioned by King Gebre Mesqel Lalibela
clues: Carved downwards out of solid volcanic rock in the shape of a cross. It stands in its own pit, about 12 metres deep.
blurb: Legend says angels helped carve the churches by night. It's one of eleven medieval churches cut from the rock at Lalibela, and still a working church.

name: Jewish Museum Berlin
clues: A zinc-clad zigzag slashed with window cuts, with empty 'voids' inside that you can see into but never enter.
blurb: The zigzag building has no entrance of its own: you go in through the Baroque building next door and down underground.

name: Turning Torso
clues: Nine five-storey cubes twist through 90 degrees up a 190-metre tower, based on its architect's sculpture of a human body.
blurb: When it opened it was the tallest building in Scandinavia. The top floor is turned a full quarter turn from the bottom one.

name: Bosco Verticale
clues: Two apartment towers with around 900 trees planted on their balconies — a forest stood on end.
blurb: Its trees and shrubs filter dust, absorb CO2 and shade the flats. Arborists abseil down the facade to prune them.

name: Shwedagon Pagoda
clues: A 99-metre gilded stupa whose tip is set with thousands of diamonds; it is said to hold strands of the Buddha's hair.
blurb: Its tip is set with thousands of diamonds and rubies, crowned by a single 76-carat diamond. Tradition says it is more than 2,500 years old.

name: Hassan II Mosque
clues: Its 210-metre minaret is one of the tallest in the world, part of the prayer hall stands over the ocean, and the roof slides open.
blurb: It holds about 25,000 worshippers inside and 80,000 more on the esplanade. A laser at the top of the minaret points towards Mecca.

name: Zeitz MOCAA
wiki: Zeitz Museum of Contemporary Art Africa
clues: Galleries carved out of the 42 concrete tubes of an old grain silo on a harbour waterfront.
blurb: The atrium was cut out of the silo's tubes in the shape of a single grain of corn. Its pillow-shaped windows glow like lanterns at night.

name: Transitional Cathedral (Cardboard Cathedral)
clues: A church built from giant cardboard tubes after an earthquake wrecked the city's old cathedral. Meant to be temporary, still standing.
blurb: The cardboard tubes are coated with waterproof polyurethane and fire retardant. Built as a stopgap, it was designed to last about 50 years.

name: Yoyogi National Gymnasium
clues: Swooping roofs hung from steel cables like a suspension bridge, built for an Olympic swimming pool.
blurb: It hosted swimming and diving at the 1964 Olympics and handball at the 2020 Games. Its sweeping roof hangs from two thick steel cables.
